hypotheses.reasoning: At 01:34:07 redis-cache was replaced and came back empty: no RDB snapshot, 0 keys (#173). Thirty seconds later search-api reported a 92% cache miss ratio, against a 3% baseline, and began loading everything from catalog-db (#177). catalog-db quickly hit CPU 100% with 483 of 500 connections in use (#180). Simple primary-key lookups (SELECT products WHERE id=$1) then took 3 to 8 seconds (#185, #202, #217). From 01:36 search-api queries started timing out at 5000ms (#192, #212), and web-bff began returning 504s on /search. Before the restart, requests were healthy at under 150ms. A cold cache alone is survivable; the damage came from every cache miss going straight to the database, which is a cache stampede.
The catalog-db connection count near its 500 limit could be read as pool exhaustion. But it only appears after the cache was wiped, so it is a symptom rather than the cause.
One translation API connection reset at 01:26 is isolated and does not line up with when the incident started. The audit_log slow query (#162) and the web-bff disk warning (#26) are also unrelated.

verdict.recommendedAction: Warm the redis cache (pre-load the most-requested products) and limit how fast cache misses can reach catalog-db: add request coalescing (one database read per missing key), rate-limit cache loads, and serve stale data where possible. Turn on RDB/AOF persistence or replicas so a replaced redis node doesn't come back empty, and add a warm-up step before a new node takes traffic.
